Their legislative elections, due on 28 November, would have been the first since January 2006, when Hamas won a parliamentary majority. It was the second time in five years he had postponed a vote. That same leadership is setting the terms of Palestinian unity. Fatah has demanded that Hamas formally accept seven political conditions laid down by Abbas as the price of national reconciliation. At talks in Cairo on 14 October, a Fatah delegation headed by Jibril Rajoub and including former Prime Minister Mohammad Shtayyeh insisted that Hamas commit itself to the political programme and agreements of the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO), which include recognition of Israel. "That is why in my talk today I am making a call for us in the Gulf to step up and take responsibility for our own security, and for us to do so inclusively." ### Netanyahu warns of Arab voter surge in Israel's election in desperate bid to woo support
- **Source**: Section Feed
- **Author**: Bilge Kotan
- **Date**: 2026-10-27 16:43
- **Link**: https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/netanyahu-warns-arab-voter-surge-israels-election-arab-leaders-call
- **Summary**: Netanyahu warns of Arab voter surge in Israel's election in desperate bid to woo support Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition partners made a last-ditch push on Tuesday to get their supporters to the polls, warning of a surging Arab voter turnout, a tactic Palestinian politicians denounced as racist and inflammatory. Cars flying Netanyahu's Likud party flags drove through Jerusalem blaring the Islamic call to prayer and urging supporters to cast their ballots because "Arabs are voting", witnesses said. "If we don't wake up now, we'll find ourselves with a government of Mansour Abbas and Ahmed Tibi," Netanyahu wrote in a post, referring to two leading Palestinian politicians in Israel. Tibi, a candidate from an Arab party, said strong turnout among Israel's Arab minority would "pave the way for an alternative government and change the grave reality". Sami Abu Shehadeh, leader of the Arab Balad party, wrote on X that long lines outside polling stations should bring "pride and joy to anyone who believed in democracy". "We are receiving all these inciting messages from the petty racists, Ben Gvir, Netanyahu, and their partners. What are they afraid of? This is actually an excellent sight, it is good for democracy."
